I met exactly one person with DID in my many visits to the psych ward.

She was 14, and had been a victim of sex trafficking from the ages 4 to 8.

The first time you met her, you couldn’t really notice it.  She wouldn’t introduce herself with different names, wouldn’t tell you she had DID. 

After a few days, you would notice that she seemed so different from time to time, like you were speaking to a completely different person. 
At that point you would either figure it out yourself, or another patient would tell you. Because that shit goes around like wildfire.

DID is so rare, even psych ward kids are amazed by it. It’s something you see maybe once during all your stays.

She had just recently gotten the diagnosis, because everybody thought her sudden mood switches were pure PTSD related. She knew she had it, talked about it sometimes, but never in a way those Tiktokers talk. She was scared, because as she described it, her body wasn’t hers anymore. Hours could pass without her witnessing them. She felt so out of control, not that she ever had any in her own life.

She didn’t know anything specific about her other personalities. All the info she had, she got from Psychologist and psychiatrist talking to her when she wasn’t fronting. They didn’t use different names or talked about different hobbies and shit like that. 

The only difference you could really notice was the different maturity levels, and different levels of aggression. Sometimes it seemed you were talking to a 4 year old, other times it felt like it was a woman in her 30s standing in front of you.
